problem: End-to-end point-goal navigation policies such as DD-PPO need billions of frames and still fail on hard episodes with u-turns and narrow passages. Modular exploration methods such as ANS and OccAnt train RL goal-selection policies tied to a single reward and do not use the uncertainty of their predictions about unobserved map regions when planning.
motivation: Both exploration and point-goal navigation require reasoning beyond the field of view. Examples are predicting whether a path leads to a dead end, or recognising that a region is already confidently mapped. Learned occupancy layout priors, together with the model's epistemic uncertainty over hallucinated regions, give a task-agnostic signal that can drive different path-selection objectives without retraining per task.
key_idea: Hallucinate top-down occupancy beyond the field of view with an ensemble of UNet predictors, then pick among RRT candidate paths using the ensemble disagreement: maximize uncertainty for exploration, or use an upper-confidence-bound traversability objective for point-goal. A pretrained DD-PPO follows the chosen short-term goals.
insight:
Using the ensemble's epistemic uncertainty as the path-selection signal works as a planning prior that makes an end-to-end local policy more robust on geometrically hard episodes.

Point-goal ablations (Table III):
- Scoring paths only by predicted occupancy (UPEN-Occ, α1=α2=0) hurts: SR is 43.8 vs 47.8 for vanilla DD-PPO on MP3D Val.
- Adding a path-length term (UPEN-Greedy) recovers SR to 48.9 on Val and 43.0 on Val-Hard.
- Adding the uncertainty bonus (full UCB, α1=0.1) gives the best SR: 49.8 on Val, 40.8 on Test and 45.7 on Val-Hard.
- The largest gain over DD-PPO (+7.7 SR) is on the high-GEDR Val-Hard set.

Exploration: FBE+DD-PPO uses the same predicted maps as UPEN, so the coverage gap (113.0 vs 85.3 m²) isolates the value of the uncertainty-maximizing objective.

SPL gains are small, and on MP3D Val SPL is even lower than DD-PPO (36.9 vs 38.7), because the policy trades path length for traversability.
method: Egocentric occupancy input: the 256×256 depth image is unprojected with camera intrinsics and ground-projected onto a 160×160 local grid (5 cm cells). Each cell takes one of three classes: unknown, occupied or free. RGB is not used.

Occupancy map predictor: a UNet with 4 encoder and 4 decoder conv blocks plus skip connections, using ResNet18 feature extraction, predicts the complete local occupancy map. It is trained with pixel-wise cross-entropy against ground truth obtained by ground-projecting MP3D scene semantics. Training pairs are sampled along shortest paths between random locations, with a variable number of accumulated depth frames. Optimizer: Adam, lr 2e-4.

Ensemble and Bayesian global maps: N=4 predictors differ only in random initialization. Each model's prediction is registered via a Bayes update into its own 768×768 global map, initialized with a uniform prior. The mean over maps gives occupancy probability and the variance gives epistemic uncertainty.

RRT candidate paths: RRT generates at most 10 paths per run, with 20% goal sampling and 5-pixel node expansion. It is re-run every 30 steps for exploration and every 20 steps for point-goal. All objectives are evaluated on the accumulated global map.
Exploration objective: choose the path maximizing the average per-cell ensemble variance along the path (Eq. 2), as a proxy for information gain and coverage.

Point-goal UCB objective: per model i, path non-traversability p_{i,s} is the maximum occupancy probability along the path. μ_s is the ensemble mean and σ_s the ensemble variance. The selected path is argmin μ_s − α1·σ_s + α2·d_s, with α1=0.1 and α2=0.5.

Local policy: the short-term goal on the selected path is given as the target to a pretrained DD-PPO agent, which outputs discrete actions. One step (map prediction, registration, RRT and DD-PPO) takes 0.37 s on average on a laptop with an i7 CPU and a GTX1060.

setting.backbone: Ensemble of 4 UNet+ResNet18 occupancy predictors (trained supervised) + RRT planner + pretrained DD-PPO local policy (used as-is)
setting.model_size: ensemble of 4 UNet/ResNet18 models (parameter count not stated)
setting.training_data: MP3D train scenes: depth/occupancy pairs sampled along shortest paths between random locations; GT occupancy from ground-projected scene semantics. DD-PPO local policy taken pretrained (not retrained).
setting.observation: egocentric depth 256×256 + agent pose (noisy odometry in default exploration setting; noise-free pose for point-goal)
setting.action_space: short-term goals on RRT paths executed by DD-PPO with low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT, TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP
setting.privileged: Point-goal uses noise-free poses from the simulator. The exploration 'noise-free' setting uses GT poses; the default exploration setting uses noisy poses with no pose estimator.

results:
Exploration on MP3D test:
- UPEN+DD-PPO covers 113.0 m² (67.9%) at T=1000. This beats FBE+DD-PPO, which uses the same predicted maps (85.3 m², 53.0%), and ANS(rgb) (73.28 m², 52.1%).
- In the noise-free setting it reaches the best Map Accuracy, 141.6 m², vs 120.2 for FBE and 104.7 for OccAnt w/o AR.
- Under pose noise its IoU (25.8%) falls below OccAnt (33.0%).

Point-goal navigation, SR vs vanilla DD-PPO:

| Set | UPEN+DD-PPO | DD-PPO |
|---|---|---|
| MP3D Val | 49.8 | 47.8 |
| MP3D Test | 40.8 | 37.3 |
| MP3D Val-Hard | 45.7 | 38.0 |

SPL gains are marginal or negative (Val: 36.9 vs 38.7).
limitations: There is no pose estimator, so under noisy poses map quality drops sharply. IoU is 25.8 vs 33.0 for OccAnt and 28.7 for FBE, even though Map Accuracy is higher.

Point-goal gains are mainly in Success. SPL is not consistently improved and is lower than vanilla DD-PPO on MP3D Val, because the policy prefers safer but longer paths. The strongest gains are shown on a custom Val-Hard set rather than an official benchmark.
Evaluation is simulation-only on MP3D with depth input. Point-goal assumes noise-free poses, and the exploration comparison covers only a few baselines.
